GCMSprime searches recovered spectra directly, preserving the fitted ion totals and using retention indices (RIs) to exclude incompatible candidates. A compiled sparse search compares hundreds of spectra against thousands of references in a fraction of a second. The same workflow supports sparse in-memory libraries and large SQLite libraries.

## One call after deconvolution

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(GCMSprime)
lib <- read_msp("library.msp", backend="sqlite", db_file="library.sqlite")
cal <- calibrate_ri("alkanes.cdf", carbon=7:23, psf=fit$psf_standard)
weights <- library_ion_weights(lib)  # compute once and reuse

identified <- identify_compounds(fit, lib, calibration=cal,
  phase="DB5", ri_tolerance=30, n_matches=5,
  method=c("stein_scott_angular", "multinomial"), ion_weights=weights,
  msp_file="sample_identified.msp", xlsx_file="sample_identified.xlsx")

identified$compounds
identified$identification$matches
```

The first method supplies the best-match columns in the compound table. Every returned match, its spectral score, RI difference, reference provenance and ion totals are included in the Excel Matches sheet. MSP output retains unique peak names, the RI, fitted pseudocount and tentative library annotation. Profiles, spectra and the model objective stay unchanged.

Identification can also run during the CDF workflow:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit <- GCMSdeco("sample.cdf", "sample.msp", xlsx_file="sample.xlsx",
  alkanes_file="alkanes.cdf", precluster=32L, library=lib,
  search=list(phase="DB5", ri_tolerance=30, n_matches=5,
              method="stein_scott"))
```

## Inspect calibration and retention constraints

```{r, eval=FALSE}
cal$anchors[, c("carbon", "start", "narrow_width", "retention_time", "RI", "residual")]
cal$candidates
```

The timing anchor is peak onset at 1% of height plus half a local narrow-peak
width. This reduces the influence of long tails on RI estimation. Standards
and sample profiles use the same convention. A natural cubic spline interpolates
the alkane coordinates and their indices exactly. `phase="DB5"` is the default;
DB1 and DBWAX are also supported. `ri_tolerance=30` admits compatible references
within 30 index units. Use a standard acquired under the sample's programme.

Unlabelled reference RIs keep their provenance. If their column class is known,
set `unknown_phase="DB5"` explicitly. `ri_tolerance=Inf` requests spectral-only
searching. [The identification theory](identification-theory.html) gives the
calibration, column matching and missing-reference rules.

RIs can also be exported without searching a library:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit <- annotate_ri(fit, cal, phase="DB5",
  msp_file="sample_RI.msp", xlsx_file="sample_RI.xlsx")
fit$compounds[c("peak_onset", "retention_coordinate", "retention_index")]
```

The MSP uses NIST's `Retention_index: SemiStdNP=...` field for a DB5-type
column. Excel retains the alkane assignments and timing coordinates. By
default, peaks outside the calibrated range receive no RI. Set
`extrapolate=TRUE` to use the natural spline's linear tails; the compound
table and MSP comments flag these values. `annotate_ri()` also annotates a
multisample result and exports median consensus RIs with the sample values.

## Choose spectral comparisons

| Method | Main use |
|:--|:--|
| `stein_scott` | Mass- and intensity-weighted dot product; the default EI comparison |
| `cosine`, `angular` | Compare spectral directions; angular gives the corresponding geometric distance |
| `hellinger` | Compare square-root-normalized ion patterns |
| `jensen_shannon`, `multinomial` | Symmetric probability/count comparisons retaining fitted query totals |
| `stein_scott_angular` | Angular distance after the Stein–Scott transform |

```{r, eval=FALSE}
w <- library_ion_weights(lib)
matches <- library_search(fit, lib, calibration=cal, phase="DB5",
  ri_tolerance=30, n_matches=5,
  method=c("stein_scott", "hellinger", "multinomial"), ion_weights=w)
as.data.frame(matches)
```

Uniform ion weights are the default. Reusable rarity weights emphasize ions
seen in fewer library spectra. Relative-intensity references with unknown ion
totals are balanced to the query total for multinomial comparisons. The
[formulas and benchmark](identification-theory.html#spectral-comparisons-and-angular-distance)
explain the transformations, weights, zero handling, score scales and accuracy.

## Identify a multisample experiment

```{r, eval=FALSE}
experiment <- GCMSdeco("chromatograms", output_dir="identified_results",
  precluster=32L, library=lib,
  search=list(phase="DB5", ri_tolerance=30, n_matches=5,
              method=c("stein_scott", "hellinger")))

occurrences <- do.call(rbind, lapply(experiment$paths,
  function(path) readRDS(path)$compounds))
occurrences <- occurrences[order(occurrences$match_score, decreasing=TRUE), ]
unique_compounds <- occurrences[!duplicated(occurrences$coupled_compound), ]
```

Library search runs on each final original-channel sample spectrum, using that
sample's alkane calibration. Consensus IDs connect repeated occurrences.
The summary above retains the best-scoring occurrence annotation per consensus
compound; full ranked matches and RI differences remain in each sample report.

See [multiple-sample deconvolution](multisample.html) for directory structure
and [spectral library import](spectral-libraries.html) for open/commercial data.
